mainTopic: When witnesses may break שבת to testify about the new moon, the source for it and its limits, and an aggadic side discussion on משה's wisdom and שלמה.
overview: The משנה teaches that witnesses who saw the new moon may break שבת to testify only for ניסן and תשרי, because those months set the dates of the ימים טובים. When the בית המקדש stood, they broke שבת for every month so the ראש חודש קרבן would be brought on time. The גמרא asks how this fits with the earlier משנה that has messengers for six months. אביי answers that all six months have messengers, but for ניסן and תשרי the messengers wait until בית דין says 'מקודש', and a ברייתא supports him. A ברייתא learns from 'אשר תקראו אותם' that שבת may be broken for declaring the month, but not so the messengers can help people keep the יום טוב. After the חורבן, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי limited breaking שבת to ניסן and תשרי. A new משנה rules that witnesses break שבת even if the moon was clearly seen. רבי יוסי disagrees, and רבן גמליאל warns רבי עקיבא not to hold back witnesses. The גמרא proves the meaning of 'בעליל' from a פסוק in תהלים, then turns to an aggadic מחלוקת between רב and שמואל about the fifty gates of understanding and whether שלמה ever matched משה.

steps.title: Breaking שבת for witnesses of ניסן and תשרי
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that witnesses may break שבת to testify about the new moon only for ניסן and תשרי, because those months set the ימים טובים and messengers are sent to סוריא for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: For two months, witnesses may break שבת: for ניסן and for תשרי. In these months messengers go out to סוריא, and through them the dates of the ימים טובים are set.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a rule: witnesses who saw the new moon may break שבת to come testify, but only for ניסן and תשרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These two months are special because the major ימים טובים fall in them: פסח in ניסן, and ראש השנה, יום כיפור and סוכות in תשרי. Getting the date right matters so much that breaking שבת to travel to בית דין is allowed. The משנה also notes that messengers go out to סוריא for these months.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (the source text being studied)
Messengers sent by בית דין to tell distant Jews the date
Syria, a nearby land outside ארץ ישראל
They set the dates of the ימים טובים

steps.confusionAlert: The people breaking שבת here are the witnesses traveling to בית דין, not the messengers. Messengers do not travel on שבת or יום טוב.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rule the גמרא will question: why does the משנה seem to say that messengers go out only for two months?

phrases.english: MISHNAH:

phrases.aramaic: עַל שְׁנֵי חֳדָשִׁים מְחַלְּלִין אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת —
phrases.english: For two months they may break Shabbat:
phrases.notes: The witnesses who saw the new moon break Shabbat by traveling to the court.

phrases.english: for Nisan and for Tishrei,
because in them messengers go out to Syria,
and through them the dates of the Festivals are set.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל שְׁנֵי חֳדָשִׁים מְחַלְּלִין אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opening of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses may break שבת to testify about the new moon only for ניסן and תשרי.

steps.title: In בית המקדש times, שבת was broken for every month
steps.stepSummary: When the בית המקדש stood, witnesses broke שבת for every month, so the ראש חודש קרבן would be brought on the right day.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the בית המקדש stood, they broke שבת for all the months, so the קרבן would be brought correctly.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds that when the בית המקדש stood, the rule was broader: witnesses broke שבת for every month.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every ראש חודש has its own קרבן (the מוסף). It has to be brought on the correct day, so each month's date needed to be set right away. Once the בית המקדש was gone, this reason fell away and only the יום טוב reason was left.

keyTerms.meaning: While the בית המקדש was standing
Even for all of them (all the months)
Making sure the קרבן is brought correctly

steps.whatToRemember: Today the rule is two months, ניסן and תשרי, because of the ימים טובים. In בית המקדש times it was all months, because of the ראש חודש קרבן.

phrases.english: And when the Temple was standing,
they would break Shabbat even for all of them (all months),
because of getting the offering right.
phrases.notes: The מוסף offering of ראש חודש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an earlier, broader version of the rule from step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In Temple times, witnesses broke שבת for every month because of the ראש חודש קרבן.

steps.title: Two months or six months?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out a contradiction: our משנה links messengers to only two months, but the earlier משנה says messengers go out for six months.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: For two months and no more?! But contrast this with the other משנה: for six months the messengers go out!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה by quoting the earlier משנה, which seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says 'in these months messengers go out', which sounds like messengers go out only for ניסן and תשרי. The earlier משנה listed six months when messengers go out: ניסן, אב, אלול, תשרי, כסלו, and אדר. So how can our משנה say only two?

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
And contrast them (one source is set against another)

phrases.english: GEMARA:
For two months and no more?!
But contrast it with this:
For six months the messengers go out!
phrases.notes: Quoted from the earlier משנה (ראש השנה 18a).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the משנה in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'שבהן שלוחין יוצאין לסוריא', which suggests messengers go out only in ניסן and תשרי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another משנה says messengers go out for six months, so it cannot be that only two months have messengers.

steps.title: אביי: the difference is when the messengers leave
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that messengers go out for all six months. For most months they leave the night before, but for ניסן and תשרי they wait until בית דין declares 'מקודש'.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: This is what the משנה means. For all the months, messengers go out from the evening. But for ניסן and תשרי, they wait until they hear בית דין say 'מקודש'.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the contradiction. He explains that the משנה is not talking about whether messengers go out, but about when they go out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the other months, once the moon was clearly seen, the messengers could leave that night, before בית דין officially declared the new month. For ניסן and תשרי, which set the תורה's ימים טובים, they had to wait for the official declaration of 'מקודש', which happened only in the daytime. Since everything waits on that declaration, it is worth breaking שבת so the witnesses arrive quickly.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the answer
This is what it means (a rereading of the text)
It is sanctified (בית דין's official declaration of the new month)

steps.confusionAlert: אביי does not say that messengers go out only for two months. All six months have messengers. Only the timing is different for ניסן and תשרי.
steps.whatToRemember: There are six months with messengers. For four of them, the messengers leave the night before. For ניסן and תשרי, they wait for בית דין's 'מקודש'.

phrases.english: Abaye said: This is what it is saying:
For all of them, messengers go out from the evening,
but for Nisan and for Tishrei,
not until they hear from the mouth of the court: 'Sanctified.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the משנה: what makes ניסן and תשרי special is the timing, not the existence of messengers.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say that messengers go out only for ניסן and תשרי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Messengers go out for all six months. For ניסן and תשרי, they leave only after בית דין declares 'מקודש'.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports אביי
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא is quoted that says exactly what אביי said, which supports his explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught in a ברייתא: For all of them, they go out from the evening. But for ניסן and תשרי, they wait until they hear בית דין say 'מקודש'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as אביי, which strengthens his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's rereading might have looked like a stretch. Now a ברייתא states that same rule outright. This confirms that the difference between the months is about when the messengers leave.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (in a ברייתא), as support
A teaching of the תנאים that was not included in the משנה

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
For all of them, they go out from the evening,
but for Nisan and for Tishrei,
not until they hear from the mouth of the court: 'Sanctified.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's answer from step 4 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's explanation that ניסן and תשרי differ only in when the messengers leave.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that states this rule word for word.

steps.title: Asking for the source that witnesses may break שבת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks where we learn that witnesses may break שבת to testify about the new moon.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: From where do we know that we may break שבת for the new months?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that asks for a source in the תורה for breaking שבת for new-moon witnesses. This question sets up the next step, where the answer comes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now we were simply told that witnesses break שבת. Breaking שבת is very serious, so the ברייתא wants a פסוק that allows it. 'מנין' means 'from where', a request for a source.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught; this introduces a ברייתא

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
From where do we know that we desecrate Shabbat for them (the new months)?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִנַּיִן שֶׁמְּחַלְּלִין עֲלֵיהֶן אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the question of which months, to the deeper question of what source allows breaking שבת at all.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that allows witnesses to break שבת for קידוש החודש.

steps.title: The verse 'which you shall declare in their time'
steps.stepSummary: The source is the פסוק 'אלה מועדי ה׳ אשר תקראו אותם במועדם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק teaches: 'These are the festivals of ה׳ which you shall declare in their appointed time.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question with a פסוק that says the מועדים must be declared at their proper time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'במועדם' (in their time) shows that the timing is required by the תורה. Because the date must be set on time, the witnesses may even break שבת to get to בית דין.

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
"These are the festivals of the Lord
which you shall declare in their appointed time."

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: אֵלֶּה מוֹעֲדֵי ה׳ אֲשֶׁר תִּקְרְאוּ אוֹתָם בְּמוֹעֲדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'אשר תקראו אותם במועדם' requires the declaration to happen on time, so it pushes aside שבת.

steps.title: Maybe שבת may also be broken so the יום טוב is kept on time
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests a possible mistake: perhaps שבת may also be broken by messengers so that people keep the יום טוב on the right day.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think: just as we break שבת so the months become sanctified, so too we break שבת so the festivals are kept properly.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a 'יכול' (one might think) idea that it will reject in the next step. This is a setup line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate jobs. One is getting the month declared (קידוש), which is the witnesses' job. The other is letting people far away know the date so they keep the יום טוב (קיום), which is the messengers' job. The suggestion is that both jobs might allow breaking שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: One might have thought (a suggestion that will be rejected)
That they are observed (kept on time)

steps.confusionAlert: 'עד שיתקדשו' and 'עד שיתקיימו' look almost the same. The first is about the witnesses getting the month declared. The second is about the messengers spreading the news so people keep the יום טוב.

phrases.english: One might think: just as we desecrate Shabbat so that the months will be sanctified,
so too we desecrate Shabbat so that the festivals will be observed on time —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whether the permission from step 7 reaches beyond the declaration itself.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the permission to break שבת also cover the messengers who announce the date so people keep the festival?

steps.title: שבת is broken for the declaration, not for the observance
steps.stepSummary: The words 'אשר תקראו אותם' limit the permission to the declaration only, not to the messengers who help people keep the festival.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק teaches 'which you shall declare them': for their declaration you may break שבת, but you may not break שבת for their observance.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא rejects the suggestion from step 8. Only the declaration of the month allows breaking שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק stresses 'תקראו' (declare), so the permission is tied to the act of declaring. The messengers who spread the news are helping with observance, so they may not break שבת. That is why the witnesses travel on שבת, but the messengers do not.
steps.whatToRemember: Witnesses may break שבת so the month gets declared (קריאה). Messengers may not break שבת so people keep the יום טוב (קיום).

phrases.english: The verse teaches: "which you shall declare them,"
for their declaration you may desecrate Shabbat,
but you may not desecrate Shabbat for their observance.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: אֲשֶׁר תִּקְרְאוּ אוֹתָם, עַל קְרִיאָתָם אַתָּה מְחַלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the 'יכול' of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. The פסוק limits breaking שבת to the declaration (קריאה), not the observance (קיום).
steps.whyThisMatters: This marks the edge of the permission. Breaking שבת is allowed only for the act the תורה requires on time, which is the declaration.

steps.title: In the בית המקדש era, שבת was broken for every month
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's line about the בית המקדש era and brings a ברייתא confirming that originally שבת was broken for all months.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: When the בית המקדש stood, they broke שבת for all the months, because of the proper timing of the קרבן. The Rabbis taught: At first they would break שבת for all the months.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה again as a heading. It then brings a ברייתא about it. This sets up the story of what changed after the חורבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a restart of step 2. The משנה's words are quoted only to attach a ברייתא to them. The ברייתא's word 'בראשונה' (at first) tells us the practice later changed.

keyTerms.meaning: Making sure the קרבן is offered properly (on the right day)

phrases.english: And when the Temple was standing —
they desecrated Shabbat even for all of the months,
because of the proper arrangement of the offering.
phrases.notes: Re-quote of the משנה (see step 2) used as a heading for the ברייתא.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה הָיוּ מְחַלְּלִין אַף עַל כּוּלָּן.
phrases.english: At first they would desecrate Shabbat even for all of the months.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְשֶׁהָיָה בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים מְחַלְּלִין אַף עַל כּוּלָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of the source and goes back to the משנה's next clause.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: While the בית המקדש stood, witnesses broke שבת for every month because of the ראש חודש קרבן.

steps.title: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי limits it to ניסן and תשרי
steps.stepSummary: After the חורבן, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי argued that with no קרבן there is no reason to break שבת every month, so it was limited to ניסן and תשרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once the בית המקדש was destroyed, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי said to them: 'Is there a קרבן now?' They enacted that שבת would be broken only for ניסן and תשרי.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its story. The reason for breaking שבת every month, the קרבן, was gone, so the rule was narrowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The every-month permission depended on the קרבן. With no קרבן, only the reason that applies to ניסן and תשרי remains: setting the dates of the major ימים טובים. This explains how the two parts of the משנה fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: The leading Sage at the time of the חורבן

steps.whatToRemember: There were two reasons to break שבת: the קרבן (every month) and the ימים טובים (ניסן and תשרי). After the חורבן only the second remains, so we break שבת only for ניסן and תשרי.

phrases.english: Once the Temple was destroyed,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶן רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי:
phrases.english: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai said to them:
Is there an offering now?
They enacted that they should not desecrate Shabbat

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא עַל נִיסָן וְעַל תִּשְׁרִי בִּלְבַד.
phrases.english: except for Nisan and Tishrei alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשֶּׁחָרַב בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ, אָמַר לָהֶן רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in step 10 and explains the change.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Today, with no קרבן, witnesses break שבת only for ניסן and תשרי, because of a תקנה of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי.

steps.title: New משנה: שבת is broken even if the moon was seen clearly
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that witnesses break שבת whether or not the moon was clearly visible to everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whether the moon was seen clearly or was not seen clearly, we break שבת for it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new question. Do witnesses still travel on שבת if the moon was so obvious that surely others saw it too?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think that if the moon was seen clearly, closer witnesses will surely come, so distant witnesses don't need to break שבת. The תנא קמא says they still break שבת in either case.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Whether the moon was seen clearly,
or whether it was not seen clearly —
we desecrate Shabbat for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ בֵּין שֶׁנִּרְאָה בַּעֲלִיל, בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא נִרְאָה בַּעֲלִיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses break שבת to testify even when the moon was clearly visible.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: no breaking שבת if the moon was seen clearly
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי disagrees and says that if the moon was seen clearly, witnesses may not break שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: If the moon was seen clearly, we do not break שבת for it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי argues on the first opinion of the משנה about a moon that was seen clearly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's reasoning is that when the moon is obvious, witnesses closer to בית דין will surely testify. Distant witnesses who travel on שבת would then be breaking שבת for no need.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
If it was seen clearly —
we do not desecrate Shabbat for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: אִם נִרְאָה בַּעֲלִיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי, when the moon was clearly seen, witnesses do not break שבת, since other witnesses will surely testify.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא holds back the witnesses in לוד
steps.stepSummary: The משנה tells a story: more than forty pairs of witnesses were traveling to testify on שבת, and רבי עקיבא stopped them in לוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was once a story where more than forty pairs of witnesses were passing through, and רבי עקיבא held them back in לוד.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a real-life story about witnesses traveling on שבת to testify about the new moon. This story sets up the next step, where רבן גמליאל responds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's reasoning was that forty pairs were far more than needed, since one pair is enough. So in his view the extra witnesses had no reason to break שבת. The story shows the real tension between avoiding needless חילול שבת and making sure enough witnesses arrive.

keyTerms.meaning: A story or incident brought as a practical example
A pair (here, a pair of witnesses)
He held them back / detained them
A town on the way to ירושלים

phrases.english: There was an incident where there passed through
phrases.notes: The witnesses were on their way to the בית דין in ירושלים.

phrases.english: more than forty pairs (of witnesses),
and Rabbi Akiva held them back in Lod.
phrases.notes: He felt they did not need to break שבת, since so many others were going.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's ruling that witnesses break שבת by giving a story where a sage limited this.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא held back extra witnesses so they would not break שבת without need.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל warns against holding back witnesses
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל sends a message to רבי עקיבא: if you stop the crowds from coming, they will not come in the future when they are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל sent him a message: If you hold back the many people, you will end up making them stumble in the future.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל objects to what רבי עקיבא did and explains the long-term danger. This closes the משנה's story with the final lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if these extra witnesses are not needed today, sending them home teaches people that their trip is pointless. Then one day, when they are truly needed, nobody will come. So the משנה's rule stays in force: witnesses should travel, even many of them.

keyTerms.meaning: You cause them to stumble (to fail)

steps.whatToRemember: The rule that witnesses break שבת for the new moon is not cut back just because there are many witnesses. Discouraging them now could leave the בית דין with no witnesses later.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key principle: a halacha sometimes looks at long-term public behavior, and not only at the needs of the moment.

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel sent to him:
If you hold back the many —
you will be found causing them to stumble in the future.
phrases.notes: They will stop coming, even when their testimony is truly needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי עקיבא's action from the previous step and gives the final lesson of the story.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Witnesses should not be held back, because doing so would discourage future witnesses.

steps.title: How do we know עליל means 'clearly seen'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that the משנה's word עליל means 'revealed' or 'clearly visible.'
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we see that this word 'עליל' is a word meaning 'revealed'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks about a word in the משנה. The משנה said 'בין שנראה בעליל,' meaning whether the moon was seen clearly. The גמרא wants a source for that meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עליל is an unusual word. The whole מחלוקת with רבי יוסי (step 13) depends on it meaning 'clearly visible to all.' So the גמרא checks the definition before relying on it.

keyTerms.meaning: From where is it implied? (a request for a source)

phrases.english: GEMARA:
phrases.notes: The גמרא's discussion of the משנה begins here.

phrases.english: From where is it implied that this word 'alil'
is a term meaning 'revealed'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מַשְׁמַע דְּהַאי עֲלִיל לִישָּׁנָא דְּמִיגַּלֵּי הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to a word in the משנה (step 12) and asks for its source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A biblical source showing that עליל means 'clearly revealed.'

steps.title: רבי אבהו proves the meaning from תהלים
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו quotes a פסוק in תהלים where בעליל describes silver refined openly, in clear view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: The פסוק says, 'The words of ה' are pure words; silver refined in clear view (בעליל) of the earth, purified seven times.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers the question by bringing a פסוק that uses the same word. In the פסוק it clearly means 'in open sight.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Refined silver is pure and shines openly, so 'בעליל לארץ' means 'visible to the whole earth.' This confirms that 'נראה בעליל' in the משנה means the moon was plainly visible. The same פסוק ends with 'שבעתים,' and that word sets up the next discussion.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק says (introducing a biblical proof)

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said: The verse states:
'The words of the Lord are pure words;
phrases.notes: תהלים 12:7

phrases.english: silver refined in clear view of the earth,
phrases.notes: Here בעליל clearly means 'openly visible.'

phrases.english: purified seven times.'
phrases.notes: This word becomes the basis for the next step (7 x 7 = 49).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק in תהלים uses בעליל to mean 'in open view,' which proves the meaning of the word.

steps.title: Fifty gates of understanding; משה received forty-nine
steps.stepSummary: Starting from the word שבעתים in the same פסוק, either רב or שמואל teaches that there are fifty שערי בינה, and משה received all except one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב and שמואל: One said, fifty gates of understanding were created in the world, and all were given to משה except one, as it says, 'You made him a little less than God.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a side topic connected to the פסוק just quoted. It brings the first view in a מחלוקת between רב and שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Purified שבעתים' is read as seven times seven, which is forty-nine levels of understanding. Since there are fifty in total, man (even משה) was made 'a little less than God,' missing exactly one gate. The second view of רב and שמואל comes in step 20.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You made him a little less than God' (תהלים 8:6)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not connected to the new moon at all. The גמרא is following the פסוק it just quoted into an aggadic side topic.

phrases.english: Rav and Shmuel: One said:
phrases.notes: We are not told which of the two said this view.

phrases.english: Fifty gates of understanding were created in the world,
and all of them were given to Moses, except for one,
phrases.notes: That is forty-nine, matching 'שבעתים' = 7 x 7.

phrases.english: as it is stated: 'And You made him a little less than God.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the word שבעתים from the פסוק that רבי אבהו quoted in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are fifty שערי בינה; משה received forty-nine of them.

steps.title: קהלת tried to equal משה and was told no
steps.stepSummary: קהלת (שלמה המלך) tried to reach משה's level, but a בת קול told him that no prophet would ever arise like משה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'קהלת sought to find words of delight' means קהלת tried to be like משה. A בת קול came out and told him: 'And written uprightly, words of truth,' meaning: 'And no prophet has arisen again in Israel like משה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the idea that משה reached the highest level a person can reach. It shows that even שלמה could not equal him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קהלת 'sought' something, which is read as trying to reach משה's level of understanding. The בת קול points to what is 'written in truth,' the תורה, where it says no prophet will rise like משה. So משה's forty-nine gates were never matched.

keyTerms.meaning: שלמה המלך, author of the book of קהלת

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next part of the רב and שמואל מחלוקת. Is משה unmatched among all people, or only among prophets?

phrases.english: 'Kohelet sought to find words of delight' —
phrases.notes: קהלת 12:10

phrases.english: Kohelet sought to be like Moses,
a heavenly voice came out and said to him:
'And written uprightly, words of truth' —
phrases.notes: This refers to what is written in the תורה.

phrases.english: 'And there has not arisen a prophet again in Israel like Moses.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 18's point that משה's level of understanding was unmatched.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even קהלת could not reach משה's level; no prophet like משה ever arose.

steps.title: The other opinion: a king did reach משה's level
steps.stepSummary: The second of רב and שמואל says that no prophet ever matched משה, but a king did: שלמה המלך.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one said: Among the prophets, no one like משה arose. Among the kings, someone did arise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second opinion in the מחלוקת. This opinion says the פסוק 'no prophet arose like משה' only talks about prophets, so a king like שלמה could still be as wise as משה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion read the פסוק 'ולא קם נביא עוד בישראל כמשה' as saying no one ever matched משה. This opinion reads the word 'נביא' narrowly: only prophets are excluded. That leaves room for שלמה המלך, who was a king, to have matched משה's wisdom.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one said: introduces the second side of a מחלוקת

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. It is the other half of the רב/שמואל מחלוקת that began in Step 18. Steps 18 and 19 together were the first side, and this is the other side.

phrases.english: And the other one said:
phrases.notes: The other one of רב and שמואל.

phrases.english: Among the prophets, none arose (like Moshe),
Among the kings, one did arise.
phrases.notes: שלמה המלך.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to Step 19 in the same מחלוקת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק only rules out a prophet equal to משה. A king, שלמה, did reach his level.

steps.title: How does this view explain 'בקש קהלת'?
steps.stepSummary: If שלמה really did reach משה's level, what does the פסוק 'קהלת sought to find' mean?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then how do I explain the פסוק 'קהלת sought to find words of delight'?
steps.whatsHappening: The second opinion now has a problem with a פסוק, and it sets up its own explanation. This line is a setup for the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 19, the first opinion used 'בקש קהלת' to mean that שלמה tried to reach משה's level and was stopped. If שלמה actually succeeded, that reading does not work. So this opinion must find a different meaning for what שלמה 'sought'.

keyTerms.meaning: But how do I uphold (explain) this פסוק? Used when a view must account for a verse that seems to go against it

phrases.english: But how do I uphold (explain)
"Kohelet sought to find words of delight"?
phrases.notes: קהלת 12:10

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises the פסוק that the first opinion relied on, which the second opinion now has to explain differently.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What did קהלת seek, if it was not to reach משה's level?

steps.title: שלמה wanted to judge by reading hearts
steps.stepSummary: קהלת wanted to judge cases based on what he knew was in people's hearts, without witnesses and without warning.
steps.simpleTranslation: קהלת sought to judge cases based on what is in the heart, without witnesses and without warning.
steps.whatsHappening: The second opinion answers: what שלמה 'sought' was not משה's level. He wanted to judge people based on his own deep understanding, skipping the usual court rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שלמה was so wise he could tell who was guilty just by understanding them. So he wanted to judge without עדים and without התראה, which the תורה normally requires. This changes 'בקש קהלת' from a story about a failed attempt to equal משה into a story about how he wanted to use his wisdom.

keyTerms.meaning: Judgments of the heart: deciding cases by inner knowledge, not by evidence
A warning given before a sin, required before a court can punish

phrases.english: Kohelet sought to judge judgments of the heart,
without witnesses and without warning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 21 with a new reading of the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: קהלת sought to judge based on his intuition, without עדים or התראה.

steps.title: A בת קול insists on two witnesses
steps.stepSummary: A heavenly voice told שלמה that judgment must follow the תורה's rule of two witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: A heavenly voice came out and said to him: "And what is written with uprightness, words of truth". That means: "By the mouth of two witnesses..."
steps.whatsHappening: A בת קול stops שלמה's plan. It quotes the end of the same פסוק and explains it as the תורה's rule that a court acts only on the word of two witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rest of the פסוק, 'וכתוב יושר דברי אמת', is read as pointing to the written תורה law of 'על פי שנים עדים'. So even the wisest judge must follow the written rules of evidence, and he may not rely on his own insight. This closes the second opinion's reading of the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is written with uprightness
By the mouth of two witnesses (דברים 17:6)

steps.whatToRemember: In one view, שלמה matched משה's wisdom, being a king and not a prophet. Even so, he was not allowed to judge by reading hearts. The תורה requires two עדים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a basic rule of Jewish courts. Punishment is based on proper testimony, not on a judge's private knowledge, no matter how wise he is.

phrases.english: A heavenly voice came out and said to him:
"And what is written with uprightness, words of truth"
phrases.notes: The end of the same פסוק in קהלת 12:10.

phrases.english: (meaning) "By the mouth of two witnesses, etc."
phrases.notes: דברים 17:6

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the reading of the פסוק by showing how שלמה's plan was rejected.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Even the wisest judge must rule by the written law of two witnesses, not by reading hearts.
